title: ASD FieldSpec3 Field Measurement Protocols
author: Margaret Kalacska
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qu7dwzn

steps.title: Power instrument and warm up
steps.instruction: Connect a 12 V battery to the FieldSpec3, turn on the instrument, and allow it to warm up for at least 30 min (each detector array warms at a different rate; insufficient warm‑up can cause spectral steps at 1000 nm and 1800 nm).

steps.title: Check fiber integrity
steps.instruction: Inspect the fiber‑optic cable with the Fibre Checker and a magnifier (manual pages 30‑32); ensure no bends are tighter than a 5‑inch diameter to avoid longitudinal fractures.

steps.title: Assemble tripods and mount grip
steps.instruction: Assemble the two tripods – place the larger tripod to hold the pistol grip and the smaller tripod to hold the Spectralon panel – and mount the pistol grip at the end of the large tripod arm.

steps.title: Connect and secure fiber cables
steps.instruction: Connect the fiber‑optic extension cable to the spectrometer’s fiber cable, tightening the screws with the small Allen key; insert the extension cable end into the pistol grip and secure with the grey nut and strain‑relief (do not overtighten; the fiber end should be visible outside the grip). Use cable ties to attach the extension cable to the tripod, avoiding tight bends that could crack the fibers.

steps.title: Attach and level Spectralon panel
steps.instruction: Attach the Spectralon panel to the small tripod using the Velcro attachment points; ensure the panel is fully level (≤ 1° tilt). Do NOT touch its surface – wear dust‑free gloves if handling is required. If dust or insects land on the panel, gently blow them away with canned air that does not contain Freon; do not brush or crush particles.

steps.title: Charge batteries and verify power
steps.instruction: Verify that both the 12 V batteries for the FieldSpec3 and the laptop batteries are fully charged before field deployment.

steps.title: Create data folder on laptop
steps.instruction: Power on the laptop, open Windows Explorer, and create a folder in the Users directory using the structure project_name/date/measurement (e.g., CABO/2018-01-01/fieldspec) where spectra will be saved.

steps.title: Connect instrument to laptop
steps.instruction: Connect the FieldSpec3 to the laptop either via its wireless network (enable the laptop’s wireless radio button, select network “16478”) or via a crossover Ethernet cable (do not substitute with a regular Ethernet cable).

steps.title: Launch RS3 and set save options
steps.instruction: Start RS 3 or RS 3 High Contrast software, choose Control → Spectrum Save, set Path Name to the folder created in the previous step, enter a Base Name (max 8 characters, record in a field notebook), set Starting Spectrum Number to 0, Number of Files to Save to 1, add optional Comments, and click OK.

steps.title: Configure foreoptic and averaging
steps.instruction: In the software select Control → Adjust Configuration, choose “Bare fibre” as the foreoptic, and set Averaging to at least 25–50 scans for dark current, white reference, and sample spectra (25 scans minimum under ideal bright conditions; 50 scans recommended for outdoor work).

steps.title: Optimize instrument before each plot
steps.instruction: With the pistol grip level and centered over the Spectralon panel, click “Opt” to let the instrument calculate the integration time; do not move the grip during optimization. The resulting DN spectrum shows detector sensitivity; repeat optimization regularly and before each plot.

steps.title: Record dark current measurement
steps.instruction: Press “DC” to acquire a dark current spectrum (critical for the VNIR detector; SWIR detectors auto‑remove DC). Perform a DC measurement every 15–20 min if no optimization has been done in that interval; note that the optimization process also records a DC.

steps.title: Collect white reference spectrum
steps.instruction: With the pistol grip still level over the Spectralon panel, click “WR” to acquire a white reference; do not move the grip or approach the panel. The saved spectrum should be a flat line at 1 (100 % reflectance). Press the space bar to save the WR spectrum.

steps.title: Measure diffuse illumination (shaded panel)
steps.instruction: Shade the Spectralon panel while keeping the pistol grip level, wait for at least one full set of scans (25–50 scans) to complete, verify the displayed spectrum is stable, then press the space bar to save the spectrum representing diffuse illumination.

steps.title: Acquire target spectra
steps.instruction: Rotate the tripod arm so the pistol grip points at the target, wait for at least one full set of scans (25–50 scans), ensure minimal steps at the detector crossover points (1000 nm and 1800 nm); if large steps appear, readjust or re‑optimize using the Spectralon panel. Press the space bar to save each spectrum; collect 5–20 spectra in rapid succession without moving the grip.

steps.title: Verify white reference after target
steps.instruction: Return the pistol grip to the centered position over the Spectralon panel, wait for a full set of scans (25–50), press the space bar to save the spectrum; it should be close to 1. Deviations indicate atmospheric or illumination changes.

steps.title: Repeat sequence for additional targets
steps.instruction: For each new target, repeat steps 11–16; optionally change the Base Name between targets to simplify QA and processing. Each space‑bar press beeps and increments the file name (e.g., Spect.001 → Spect.002).

steps.title: Account for FOV and atmospheric noise
steps.instruction: Remember the instrument’s 25° field of view (bare fibre); calculate spot size from the fibre height, note detector sensitivity is non‑uniform within the FOV, and ensure the target area is homogeneous and larger than the instantaneous FOV. Expect normal high noise at 1400 nm and 1900 nm caused by atmospheric water absorption.
